label: rem:jet-planck-particle-spectrum
title: Particle spectrum per Planck step
html:
The equivalence between Planck time and jet prolongation reveals the sequential unfolding of the particle spectrum at the Big Bang. Each tick of time supplies exactly enough algebraic degree to resolve one higher crossing number. The knot complexity of a particle dictates the precise Planck step when it first becomes topologically possible.

Step 0: the photon. At t = 0, the initial state is the zero jet J^0E. This encodes only the value at a point: position is known exactly, momentum is completely unknown. No horizontal transport has occurred. The zero jet carries the empty braid word — the identity element \mathbf{1}, the trivial Hecke representation with no crossings and no closed strand (the empty knot \varnothing). This is distinct from the unknot 0_1, which is a closed strand and belongs to the neutrino at step 1. The photon corresponds to the zero-jet state: it is the particle of zero rest mass, pure energy, and no topological constraint.

Step 1: the neutrino and antineutrino. The first application of the Reeb derivation \nabla_q yields the 1-jet J^1E. The derivative establishes correlation between neighboring fibers. This allows a single full twist: a knot with one apparent crossing (which can be untwisted to the unknot, but requires one algebraic step to evaluate). This is the neutrino \nu = T_{1,0} and the antineutrino \nu^{\sigma} = T_{1,0}^{\sigma}. The neutrino is the lightest matter, the minimum topological excitation above the photon vacuum.

Step 2: the Hopf link (bosons). The Hopf link L2a1 comprises two unknots linked once. The linking number is 1, which requires detecting curvature. This is exactly the Hessian d^2E: the quadratic jet detects the first non-trivial holonomy. Bosons are links with an even number of components. The simplest is T(2,2) = L2a1 (gluon), existing at step 2. The gluon is its own antiparticle because the Hopf link is amphichiral. At step 2, there is no chirality. The quadratic jet has a discriminant but no handedness.

Step 3: chirality, the electron, and the positron. The trefoil 3_1 = T_{2,3} has crossing number 3. Its braid word requires three R-matrix evaluations. It cannot exist before the cubic jet. Step 3 introduces chirality. The left trefoil T_{2,3} and the right trefoil T_{2,3}^{\sigma} are distinct. This originates the particle-antiparticle distinction for chiral matter:

  • Electron e^- = T_{2,3}
  • Positron e^+ = T_{2,3}^{\sigma}

Both appear at the same Planck step. The cubic jet produces both chiralities simultaneously. The same step produces the up quark (u = T_{2,3}) and down quark (d = T_{2,3}^{\sigma}) as the same trefoil pair in the color-tube sector.

Step 4: the Higgs mass mechanism and the first hadrons. The figure-eight knot 4_1 has crossing number 4 and is the first hyperbolic knot. It is amphichiral, so the Higgs field H is its own antiparticle. The Borromean baryon \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}) also emerges at step 4. Although each constituent quark has crossing number 3, the three-component Borromean linking requires the quartic jet to resolve the inter-component holonomy. The proton p, neutron n, and their antiparticles first appear here.

Step 5: the muon and heavy quarks. The cinquefoil 5_1 = T_{2,5} has crossing number 5 and genus 2. It is chiral, producing:

  • Muon \mu^- and antimuon \mu^+
  • Charm quark c and strange quark s

The muon and antimuon share the same torus knot type but are distinguished by chirality.

Summary: the unfolding. See Table 2.

The universe unfolds through successive jet approximations. The crossing number c(K) is the computational cost in Planck steps. A universe at step n can resolve knots with c \leq n but not those with c > n.
